security_audit.summary: The static backtick, URL, and SQLite path findings are false positives caused by Markdown documentation and code examples. I found one semantic risk: the skill recommends unpinned npx agentdb@latest commands that can execute changing package code.

remediation.suggestion: Pin AgentDB commands to a reviewed version and tell users to confirm package source before execution.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Package Execution Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells users to run npx agentdb@latest commands. Using latest can execute package code that changes after publication.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands are explicit user-facing npx invocations with an @latest version selector. This is a supply-chain risk, although not evidence of malicious intent.

content.value_statement: AgentDB teams need faster vector search and lower memory use as datasets grow. This skill provides tuning guidance for quantization, HNSW indexing, caching, batching, and monitoring.
actual_capabilities: Explains binary, scalar, product, and full-precision quantization tradeoffs.
Guides HNSW parameter choices for small, medium, large, and massive datasets.
Shows caching and batch-operation patterns for faster AgentDB retrieval workflows.
Provides monitoring checks for database size, latency, confidence, and cache hit rate.
Offers optimization recipes for speed, accuracy, memory limits, and production scaling.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not automatically change an AgentDB database.
It assumes Node.js, AgentDB, and an existing vector workload are available.
Performance results depend on hardware, embeddings, dataset size, and recall targets.
The examples use npx commands that should be reviewed before execution.

use_cases.title: Reduce Vector Storage Costs
use_cases.description: Plan quantization and cache settings for a growing AgentDB collection while preserving acceptable retrieval accuracy.

use_cases.title: Improve Retrieval Latency
use_cases.description: Tune HNSW search, result counts, and cache behavior for an AI application with slow nearest-neighbor queries.

use_cases.title: Prepare Production Benchmarks
use_cases.description: Create repeatable benchmark and monitoring steps before scaling AgentDB to hundreds of thousands of vectors.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Starter Optimization
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my AgentDB workload. Recommend a first optimization plan for vector count, memory limits, accuracy needs, and latency targets.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Quantization Settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare binary, scalar, product, and no quantization for my dataset. Explain memory savings, accuracy tradeoffs, and test priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Search Latency
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my AgentDB search latency. Recommend HNSW, cache, and batch settings for this vector count and recall target.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Production Scaling
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production optimization plan for one million AgentDB vectors. Include benchmark steps, rollback checks, monitoring metrics, and supply-chain precautions.

output_examples.input: A product search app has 500,000 embeddings and high memory use.
output_examples.output: A recommendation to test scalar quantization, set a measured cache size, benchmark recall, and monitor search latency before production.

output_examples.input: A support retrieval system has slow nearest-neighbor queries.
output_examples.output: A tuning plan for HNSW parameters, smaller result sets, cache hit-rate tracking, and benchmark comparisons against the baseline.

output_examples.input: An edge app needs local vector search with limited RAM.
output_examples.output: A tradeoff review for binary quantization, reduced cache size, small HNSW connections, and accuracy validation on representative queries.

best_practices: Benchmark a baseline before changing quantization, HNSW, cache, or batch settings.
Validate recall and accuracy after each performance change with representative queries.
Pin command versions and review packages before running npx examples.
anti_patterns: Do not choose binary quantization when exact recall is required.
Do not increase HNSW quality settings without measuring build time and memory.
Do not trust headline speedups without testing on your own workload.

faq.question: Does this skill execute commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It is documentation, but some examples ask users to run npx commands.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Do I need an existing AgentDB database?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is most useful when you have vectors, queries, and performance goals.

faq.question: Can it guarantee the benchmark speedups?
faq.answer: No. Results depend on hardware, vector count, embedding dimensions, and accuracy requirements.

faq.question: What should I optimize first?
faq.answer: Start with baseline benchmarks, then test quantization, cache size, and HNSW settings separately.

faq.question: Is this only for large datasets?
faq.answer: No. It also covers small and medium deployments that need predictable latency.
